name: Autologous conditioned serum

card.summary: An injectable serum made from a person's own blood, rich in interleukin-1 receptor antagonist, used for joint and tissue inflammation and explored for jaw-joint comfort and skin rejuvenation.
card.note: Clinic-based injection; not FDA approved in the US.

quick.overview:
Autologous conditioned serum (ACS), sold as Orthokine, is made by incubating a person's blood and separating the serum, which is then rich in anti-inflammatory proteins such as interleukin-1 receptor antagonist. It is injected into inflamed joints or tissues.

Its link to appearance runs through recovery and comfort: calmer joints and tendons can support continued training, and jaw-joint (TMJ) injections are studied by oral surgeons. A separate blood-derived product has also been studied for skin aging.
quick.how: In clinics, blood is drawn, incubated and centrifuged, and the resulting serum is injected over a series of sessions into the target joint or area. It is performed by physicians; it is not a home practice.
quick.risks: As an injection it carries the usual procedural risks. The US FDA has not approved it, and a Wikipedia summary reports tentative evidence overall. Trials in knee osteoarthritis and TMJ conditions are the main published human data.

lead: Autologous conditioned serum (ACS), also called Orthokine, is a blood-derived injectable. Blood is incubated and centrifuged to yield serum enriched in interleukin-1 receptor antagonist, a natural inhibitor of an inflammatory cytokine. It was developed in the mid 1990s and used in osteoarthritis, radicular pain and some tendon and muscle injuries [1].

In the hardmaxx context its relevance is indirect: it is discussed as a way to settle inflamed joints and tendons so people can keep training and recover from procedures. It has also been studied in jaw-joint (temporomandibular) conditions [2][3].

The best-known trial randomized 376 people with knee osteoarthritis to ACS or placebo and reported on pain and function outcomes [4]. A multicenter study of a related cell-free blood secretome product, Exokine, examined skin aging [5].

chain: Own blood incubated to enrich IL-1Ra
Serum injected at inflamed joint or tendon
Less joint inflammation allows continued training and recovery
angle.text: ACS targets inflammation in joints and soft tissue, which people in strength and jaw-surgery circles connect to recovery and keeping up training. A blood-secretome product from the same family has been tested for skin aging.

paras: About 60 ml of blood is drawn, incubated at slightly raised temperature and centrifuged; the serum is injected into the affected area. The treatment is often given as a series [6].
A review describes use for human and equine osteoarthritis and radicular compression, with interest in tendinopathy, muscle injury and tunnel widening after ACL reconstruction [1].

A 2024 pilot randomized study compared ACS with dextrose prolotherapy in TMJ internal derangement [2], and a 2026 randomized trial compared ACS with platelet-rich plasma after arthrocentesis in TMJ osteoarthritis [3].
A multi-center prospective study of Exokine, a cell-free blood cell secretome, reported on skin aging parameters [5].

Wikipedia states the evidence is tentative, that ACS was first approved in Germany in 2003, has no FDA approval, and cost about 6,000 euros in 2012 [6]. A 2019 review of orthobiologics for osteoarthritis places ACS alongside PRP and other products [7].

The randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled knee osteoarthritis trial enrolled 376 patients [4]. Other randomized work compares ACS with triamcinolone in knee osteoarthritis and with other injections in TMJ disorders [2][3]. Case series have examined trigeminal neuralgia.

timeline.event: ACS developed as a source of IL-1Ra [1]
